assessment: Current CPU retained-cache LL14 profile; classical security screen, not a proof
conclusion: Dense families narrowly pass BDGL16 but fail 128 under MATZOV. Retune with margin and requalify accuracy/performance before claiming 128-bit security. These are Gaussian-proxy attack-cost estimates, not exact security levels or demonstrated attacks.

profile.sparse_secret: One uniform position and independent random sign per public block; 30 blocks of width 529 and one of width 514; h=31

noise_scope: sampleNoise truncates a continuous normal toward zero. RMS values use the ideal-normal integer second moment. The estimator instead models a variance-matched discrete Gaussian; the exact PMF and finite-precision PRNG effects are not assessed.

reports.scope:
Structured ring joint-decoding sensitivity from posterior rotation histograms.

Compares common decoding outcomes, conditional decoding independence, and an
optimistic union bound. None establishes actual correlations or security.
The full square-root speedup on labelled dictionaries remains a heuristic.
reports.noise_proxy: DiscreteGaussian with supplied integer RMS; exact sampler distribution is not modeled
reports.probability_reuse_scope: Posterior matching histogram depends on the unchanged secret/guessing geometry; decoder probabilities are recomputed at the selected modulus and noise

posterior_uncertainty.simultaneous_scope: All decoder marginals and beta/d choices using this same fixed-layout posterior histogram
posterior_uncertainty.expectation_bound: epsilon for 1/K; p*epsilon for h_p(K)=(1-(1-p)^K)/K by monotone summation by parts
posterior_uncertainty.excludes: Other layouts, weights, zeta, seeds, decoding-correlation hypotheses, and security certification

limitations: Decoder marginal uses scalar GSA Babai and MITM probabilities; actual cross-rotation correlations unmodeled
Conditional decoder independence and optimistic union bound are sensitivities, not established attacks
Only one zeta/layout/weight and supplied beta/d offsets; no global optimum
Full square-root work on labelled dictionaries assumed; compatible decompositions not constructed
Posterior finite-sample uncertainty is not a security confidence interval
Candidate modulus overrides do not establish matching C++ accuracy or exposed-key security
Correlated evaluation keys remain unqualified

structured_sensitivity.scope: Bounded grid, weights 9..15, fixed zeta=14688 and saturated-5-prefix layout; no global minimum or security lower bound. Histograms have 4000 posterior samples each, seed 2119. Geometry-only histograms are reused; decoder probabilities are recomputed at q56 and RMS 2.8283. The iid95 limits describe the posterior model only, not confidence in security. An additional weight15 beta/d boundary grid found no cheaper tested point.

limitations: Generic sparse proxy fixes 16 positive and 15 negative coefficients and omits public block constraints; actual block secret has independent signs.
Sparse proxy evaluated only under BDGL16; no full MATZOV uniform-sparse run.
No complete analysis of exact error PMF, ring/KDM or correlated evaluation-key samples.
Structured decoder correlations and full square-root speedup for labelled dictionaries remain heuristic; different weights, masks, layouts and zeta values remain unsearched.
Unbounded generic samples and maximum beta 4096; reported attack costs are model dependent.
